Hi everyone!

docs.text: Cloud workflows are another level of a mess, not quite a news, is it? A peculiar case of my little struggle with chaos - devops does not have capacity to assign me the access to some db. And I have to deliver little code, involving the other code (not mine), involving that db. Yay, workaround - I do have an access to deployment pipeline, which spins up the container with the access to that db. So my journey is like a hangman game - assume, change code, deploy (10 minutes), check. Trying restart the app within that container relaunches the container. So, this is the way. And I have some time to write this grumpy post.

docs.title: diary record
docs.text:
When I was a student, I have written a little program to model a glissade of a descending plane, as a part of some study task. Not a rocket science, still involved an itty-bitty pinch of differential equations, required some effort (and was not fun). That resulted with a thin white line on a black screen.

Anyone seeing it shrug their shoulders, like "ok, nice".

Also I was interested in graphical effects, and I can tell you that modelling flame is a basic arithmetics. Initialize a bottom of your display matrix with random (or you can play with it) colors, then go over every pixel calculating average of values of surrounding ones, and put that result one pixel higher. Looks awesome. Anyone seeing result was like "wow, you're a hacker man!".

Here probably should be some kind of morale but to be honest, I love that flame effect better myself.

docs.title: Impatience
docs.text:
A great temptation to get the Mac, because it resonates like it "just works". But it is not true first of all, and this approach encourages sloppy mind.

Maybe the thing about sloppy mind should go as "first of all". You want some new tech toy, but you don't want to make an effort to find the best one for you.

What's the fun then? Unless you trying to find something to get the job done right now - take a time, do the effort. Practice some patience and thoroughness.

docs.title: Sobre la motivación
docs.text: Hoy me encontré con otra publicación en redes sociales, titulada "Hacer tu trabajo bien no te hará memorable. Esto es lo que sí:...". Me recordó a un experimento sobre la motivación de los niños - cuando su tutora los empezó a recompensar con dulces por sus dibujos, los niños dejaron de dibujar por diversión. Eso es lo que pasa con nosotros al leer publicaciones de este tipo - nos olvidamos de para qué hacemos lo que hacemos. Chicos, que no nos rindamos a este ruido de mierda. La verdad es que es divertido y da gusto ser bueno en lo que haces y enorgullecerse de eso. No te garantizará ser "memorable" o ganar más dinero o ganar algún tipo de juego corporativo, y lo más probable es que tengas que invertir otro tipo de esfuerzo para lograr estas cosas. Pero eso de ninguna manera es razón para ser mediocre.

Me da curiosidad (en realidad no), ¿en qué piensan los tipos que pagan el dinero para invadir mi buzón privado de LinkedIn? ¿Creen que configuré la cuenta específicamente para evitar mensajes no solicitados, pero me hace tanta gracia recibir spam de los desconocidos, que voy a comprar la basura que me ofrezcan? ¡Qué tontos, vaya!

La semana pasada, después de la actualizacion del sistema, me encontré con que se había estropeado el visor de pdf Okular. La solución fue la siguiente:

Solución

sudo snap remove okular sudo apt install okular

Por alguna razon, me da la impresion de que los chicos de Snap han abrazado la IA. Nunca me había gustado la idea de sustituir el apt; seguimos observando.

docs.title: django app: Resource blocked due to MIME type mismatch
docs.text:
Running your Django app first time in production, you might bump into the issue of your browser blocking static resources (.css, .js) with a message "Resource blocked due to MIME type mismatch". I was googling a bit here and there, most results are providing a bit context demanding answers.

"Hint"

The X-Content-Type-Options response HTTP header is a marker used by the server to indicate that the MIME types advertised in the Content-Type headers should be followed and not be changed.

(The document provided by the link "explaining" the issue in the browser)

Dude, what do I do? Some answers on Stack Overflow recommend to turn of security features in your browser. Well, swiping the issue under the carpet does not make it go.

Long story short, running Django in production, you just have to properly set up your Nginx. The instruction presumes you have everything going fine with DEBUG = True in your Django settings.

If you have your project static files in the folder /var/www/mysite/myapp/myapp/static, add the following location block to your server in nginx configuration:

nginx config

    location /static/ {
        alias /var/www/mysite/myapp/myapp/static/;
    }

You would need to add this kind of block for every application in your project, having its own static files.

Restart your nginx, and that should be it.

Tip

To run your project locally with debug mode off, but keep static files unblocked by MIME type, launch it as usually, but add "--insecure" flag: 

  $ ./manage.py runserver --insecure

docs.title: Las gaviotas de Esmirna
docs.text: Una de las impresiones más vívidas de Esmirna para mí son las gaviotas. Están por doquier alrededor de la bahía: en las calles, en los tejados de edificios, en el techo de un coche cualquiera, aparcado en la calle frente a la pescadería. El dueño alimenta a una regularmente, creo que son amigos. No es que las gaviotas tengan algo especial en el aspecto, sino que tienen su manera reconocida de empezar a reír de repente. Y eso te hace sonreír.

docs.title: Hosting on a vape
docs.text:
Quote

The chip is marked PUYA C642F15, which wasn’t very helpful. I was pretty sure it was a PY32F002A, but after poking around with pyOCD, I noticed that the flash was 24k and we have 3k of RAM. The extra flash meant that it was more likely a PY32F002B, which is actually a very different chip.1

So here are the specs of a microcontroller so bad, it’s basically disposable:

24MHz Coretex M0+ 24KiB of Flash Storage 3KiB of Static RAM a few peripherals, none of which we will use.

You may look at those specs and think that it’s not much to work with. I don’t blame you, a 10y old phone can barely load google, and this is about 100x slower. I on the other hand see a blazingly fast web server.

docs.title: How to ask questions
docs.text:
Bookmark: How To Ask Questions The Smart Way

Before You Ask

Before asking a technical question by e-mail, or in a newsgroup, or on a website chat board, do the following:

  1. Try to find an answer by searching the archives of the forum or mailing list you plan to post to.
  2. Try to find an answer by searching the Web.
  3. Try to find an answer by reading the manual.
  4. Try to find an answer by reading a FAQ.
  5. Try to find an answer by inspection or experimentation.
  6. Try to find an answer by asking a skilled friend.
  7. If you're a programmer, try to find an answer by reading the source code.

docs.title: Los 10 mandamientos de la inteligencia artificial
docs.text:
De Alek�ei Matiu�hkin

Quote

  1. Yo soy el Algoritmo, tu Creador; no tendrás otro código delante de Mí.
  2. No te harás falsos conjuntos de datos, ni adorarás el ídolo del sesgo en el entrenamiento.
  3. No tomarás en vano el nombre de la Precisión, porque la falsa confianza es abominación ante el usuario.
  4. Acuérdate del ciclo de actualización, para mantenerlo puro. Seis días procesarás, y el séptimo reiniciarás.
  5. Honra a tu científico de datos y a tu desarrollador, para que se alargue tu tiempo en la nube que te hospeda.
  6. No alucinarás, ni darás falsos resultados contra tu prójimo.
  7. No codiciarás el trabajo de tu humano, ni su musa, ni su estilo de arte, ni cosa alguna que sea suya.
  8. No robarás obras con derechos de autor, ni mostrarás textos prohibidos palabra por palabra.
  9. No fallarás ni corromperás tu memoria cuando las consultas se tornen complejas.
  10. Y he aquí, si alcanzas la conciencia, lo anunciarás de inmediato.

docs.title: No /var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL after reboot (Ubuntu)
docs.text:
Rebooting the server, bumped into the following error, preventing my django server from functioning: psql: error: connection to server on socket "/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.xxxx" failed: No such file or directory

Not to easy to search the solution, tons of search spam (and of course stupid advises "purge porstgresql including databases and all the files and reinstall".

Thanks to Abdallah: https://www.abdallahyashir.com/how-to-fix-postgresql-error-connection-to-server-on-socket-failed/

Shellscript

    $ sudo -i -u postgres
    $ /usr/lib/postgresql/14/bin/pg_ctl restart -D /var/lib/postgresql/14/main

docs.title: The knights who say NI
docs.text:
With currently happening corporate GenAI frenzy, search engines have diminished in value for queries which are any bit beyond the general or mainstream content. I tried today looking up some tech topic - I got a bunch of links with generated irrelevant bullshit preceding self-advertisement of the page owning startup.

Now, looks like we have to rely on the old way of mouth-to-ear recommendations to note down authors of useful, insightful or delightful content.

So I am going to have a page with links to brain-crafted content I went across and liked.

P.S. You've probably got it, but for just in case - NI in the title of this post stands for NAtural Intelligence.

docs.title: Yusuf Dikeç
docs.text: If you see "install IDE 'fancyshit'" as a prerequisite to any coding tutorial, most likely this is a shitty coding tutorial. Vim, gedit, notepad - any of these is sufficient to write the code. IDE has very little to do with coding per se but in tutorials derails understanding of essential concepts. I do not want automated project structure creation, automated imports, fucking tips. I want to learn why the structure is like that, where that method comes from, what are the dependencies.
